name: elopement
text: elopement is the standard English translation of the Irish Aíthéd. Aíthéd stands as the first word of a recognised tale category in Old and Middle Irish literature. A well-known example is Aíthéd Finn, or The Elopement of Fionn. Writers occasionally misuse elopement as a translation of Tóraigheacht, which actually means pursuit. The two tale-types share narrative surface but name distinct genres. The English term thus sits at the hinge of two related Irish tale categories.

attributes.attribute: English translation of the Irish tale-category word Aíthéd, with Aíthéd Finn as a primary example.
Occasionally misapplied to Tóraigheacht, the Irish word for pursuit.

okr.objective: Document elopement as the English translation of the Irish tale-category word Aíthéd and note its occasional confusion with Tóraigheacht.
key_results: Names elopement as the English rendering of the Irish Aíthéd.
Cites Aíthéd Finn (The Elopement of Fionn) as the primary example of the tale category.
Notes the occasional mistranslation of Tóraigheacht (pursuit) as elopement.
